scenario_text: Track an acute outbreak in a closed, normalized population divided into susceptible, infectious, and recovered fractions. New infections transfer individuals from the susceptible fraction to the infectious fraction through homogeneous person-to-person contact, while recovery transfers infectious individuals to the recovered fraction. The symbolic regression target is the instantaneous change in infectious prevalence over time. Observations span the rise, peak, and decline of a single outbreak under fixed transmission and recovery conditions.
baseline_mechanisms: Transmission generated by encounters between susceptible and infectious population fractions.
Recovery that removes individuals from the infectious fraction at a constant per-capita rate.
Compartment transfers that preserve the total normalized population.
baseline_assumptions: The population is closed to births, deaths, immigration, and emigration during the observation window.
Contacts are homogeneous, with no age, spatial, or behavioral structure.
Recovered individuals remain immune for the full observation window.
Transmission and recovery conditions are constant over time.
scientific_constraints: All state fractions must remain non-negative.
The susceptible, infectious, and recovered fractions must sum to one at all times.
Transmission cannot occur when either the susceptible or infectious fraction is zero.
Recovery can only decrease the infectious fraction and increase the recovered fraction.
refinement_agenda: Add time-varying transmission to represent behavioral changes or control measures.
Introduce a latent infected state to represent a noninfectious incubation period.
Allow immunity to wane so recovered individuals can return to susceptibility.
Add disease-associated mortality or demographic turnover when the closed-population assumption is relaxed.

domain_mechanisms.description: contact or transmission response changes with prevalence or density
risk response changes contact or control behavior
finite immunity duration or recovery transition

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of the infectious population fraction.

required_dynamic_states.description: Fraction of the population susceptible to infection.
Fraction of the population currently infectious.
Fraction of the population recovered and immune.

expected_behaviors: Infectious prevalence increases when transmission into the infectious class exceeds recovery.
Susceptible prevalence is non-increasing while infectious individuals remain present.
Recovered prevalence is non-decreasing.
The outbreak reaches a finite prevalence peak and then declines when susceptible availability becomes sufficiently low.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative susceptible, infectious, or recovered fractions.
A total population fraction that changes over time.
Spontaneous growth of infection when the infectious fraction is zero.
Direct loss from the susceptible class without a corresponding gain in the infectious class.

scenario_text: Model short-term arterial pressure regulation after the circulation begins away from its resting operating point. Mean arterial pressure changes through the imbalance between cardiac delivery and peripheral runoff, while autonomic vasomotor drive is adjusted by pressure-sensitive feedback and relaxes toward a pressure-dependent command level. Posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and circulating hormone levels remain fixed background conditions during the observation window. The scientific target is the instantaneous rate of change of mean arterial pressure along the coupled pressure-control trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Arterial pressure changes according to the balance between cardiac delivery into the arterial compartment and pressure-dependent peripheral runoff.
Autonomic vasomotor drive modulates effective cardiac delivery and peripheral resistance.
Pressure-sensitive neural feedback sets a bounded autonomic command that decreases as arterial pressure rises.
Autonomic vasomotor drive relaxes toward its commanded level with a finite physiological response time.
baseline_assumptions: The arterial circulation is represented as one well-mixed compliant compartment.
Posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and circulating vasoactive hormones are constant.
Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window.
scientific_constraints: Mean arterial pressure must remain nonnegative.
Normalized autonomic vasomotor drive must remain between zero and one.
The autonomic feedback command must be nonincreasing with arterial pressure.
Peripheral runoff must be nonnegative and must not decrease when pressure rises under otherwise fixed conditions.
refinement_agenda: Add a finite neural conduction and effector delay if transient oscillations are systematically missed.
Separate cardiac and vascular autonomic effectors when their recovery times differ.
Allow arterial compliance to vary with pressure if large excursions show asymmetric relaxation.
Add a slowly adapting pressure-sensor operating point for longer experiments.
Release the fixed blood-volume assumption by introducing a measured hemorrhage or infusion disturbance.

domain_mechanisms.description: negative feedback around a physiological set point
finite storage, transport, or organ capacity

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of mean arterial pressure in millimeters of mercury per second.

required_dynamic_states.description: Mean arterial pressure in millimeters of mercury.
Normalized autonomic vasomotor drive, with zero representing minimal drive and one representing maximal drive.

expected_behaviors: Pressure below its regulated operating region increases autonomic vasomotor drive.
Pressure above its regulated operating region decreases autonomic vasomotor drive.
Autonomic drive approaches its pressure-dependent command level over a finite response time.
For physiologically moderate perturbations, pressure and autonomic drive return toward a stable resting state without sustained divergence.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative arterial pressure.
Autonomic vasomotor drive outside its normalized physiological interval.
A feedback direction in which elevated pressure persistently increases vasomotor drive.
Unbounded pressure growth under fixed baseline conditions.

scenario_text: A single cell is stimulated under fixed extracellular conditions, causing calcium to cycle between the cytosol and the endoplasmic reticulum. Calcium-dependent channel activation promotes store release, while slower channel inactivation limits continued release and enables recovery. ATP-driven uptake returns cytosolic calcium to the store, allowing repeated pulses or damped oscillations from different initial intracellular states. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of cytosolic calcium along the resulting time trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Calcium-dependent opening of endoplasmic-reticulum release channels.
Calcium-dependent inactivation and recovery of release-channel availability.
Saturable uptake of cytosolic calcium into the endoplasmic reticulum.
Passive calcium leakage from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cytosol.
baseline_assumptions: The cytosol and endoplasmic reticulum are each spatially well mixed.
Extracellular stimulation is constant throughout a trajectory.
Mitochondrial calcium handling and plasma-membrane calcium fluxes are negligible.
Effective compartment volumes and calcium-buffering capacities are constant.
scientific_constraints: C and S must remain nonnegative.
The channel-availability state h must remain between zero and one.
Every baseline flux between the cytosol and endoplasmic reticulum must enter the two compartment balances with opposite directions.
In the absence of external fluxes, total intracellular calcium adjusted for fixed compartment capacities must be conserved.
refinement_agenda: Add stimulus-dependent calcium influx across the plasma membrane and calcium extrusion from the cell.
Introduce dynamic mitochondrial calcium uptake and release.
Replace constant buffering capacity with calcium-dependent cytosolic buffering.
Allow spatial gradients between local release sites and bulk cytosol.
Add stochastic release-channel opening for low-copy-number channel clusters.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

spec.target_description: Time derivative of free cytosolic calcium concentration.

required_dynamic_states.description: Free cytosolic calcium concentration in micromolar.
Free endoplasmic-reticulum calcium store concentration in micromolar.
Fraction of calcium-release channels available for activation.

expected_behaviors: Cytosolic calcium remains nonnegative and may exhibit repeated or damped pulses.
Store depletion reduces calcium release and is followed by recovery through uptake.
Channel availability decreases during elevated cytosolic calcium and recovers when cytosolic calcium falls.
Release and uptake produce opposing changes in cytosolic and store calcium.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative calcium concentrations or channel-availability fractions outside zero to one.
Calcium release continuing at a substantial rate when the intracellular store is depleted.
Unbounded growth of cytosolic or store calcium in the closed baseline system.
Independent sampling of C, S, or h at each time point rather than joint trajectory evolution.

scenario_text: An enzyme interconverts between low-activity and high-activity conformations, with a small-molecule activator favoring the high-activity state. Initial reaction rates are measured across independently varied substrate and activator concentrations while enzyme abundance, pH, and temperature remain fixed. The benchmark should recover how substrate occupancy and activator-controlled conformational selection jointly determine the instantaneous catalytic rate. Measurements are restricted to the initial-rate regime so product accumulation and substrate depletion are negligible.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible substrate occupancy of catalytic sites
Activator binding that shifts the enzyme population toward a more catalytically competent conformation
Catalytic turnover by substrate-bound enzyme
baseline_assumptions: Total enzyme concentration is fixed and much lower than substrate concentration.
Binding and conformational populations equilibrate rapidly relative to the initial-rate measurement.
Product concentration is negligible, so reverse conversion and product inhibition are absent.
All catalytic sites experience identical fixed pH and temperature conditions.
scientific_constraints: The predicted rate must remain nonnegative.
The rate must vanish in the absence of substrate.
Finite enzyme abundance imposes a bounded maximum conversion rate.
Activator occupancy and catalytic-site occupancy must remain between zero and full occupancy.
refinement_agenda: Add substrate inhibition caused by binding to a secondary inhibitory site at high substrate concentration.
Allow the activator to alter both substrate affinity and catalytic turnover rather than only conformational occupancy.
Introduce competitive product inhibition when initial-rate conditions are relaxed.
Represent slow conformational relaxation explicitly if rapid equilibration fails.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Initial substrate conversion rate per unit assay volume
expected_behaviors: The rate is nonnegative throughout the sampled domain.
At fixed activator concentration, increasing substrate raises the rate toward a finite plateau.
At fixed substrate concentration, increasing activator raises the rate toward an activator-dependent limit.
The activator has little additional effect once conformational activation is nearly complete.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative catalytic rates
Unbounded rate growth at high substrate concentration
A sustained decrease in rate as activator concentration increases
A nonzero conversion rate when substrate concentration is zero

scenario_text: A closed habitat contains a prey population and a specialist predator population observed over time. Prey increase through reproduction but are removed by predator encounters, while predators decline naturally and reproduce in proportion to prey consumed. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of prey abundance along a joint population trajectory. Environmental conditions and habitat area remain fixed throughout each observation window.
baseline_mechanisms: Prey reproduction proportional to current prey abundance.
Prey removal through mass-action encounters between prey and predators.
Predator natural mortality proportional to current predator abundance.
Predator recruitment proportional to successful prey consumption.
baseline_assumptions: The habitat is closed to immigration and emigration.
The predator feeds only on the modeled prey population.
Per-capita demographic and encounter parameters remain constant over time.
Predator handling limits and prey crowding are negligible over the modeled abundance range.
scientific_constraints: Both population states remain nonnegative from nonnegative initial conditions.
Predation contributes a nonpositive term to prey change and a nonnegative contribution to predator recruitment.
Predator abundance cannot increase through consumption when prey abundance is zero.
The zero-abundance boundary for either population cannot be crossed into negative values.
refinement_agenda: Add prey self-limitation when crowding becomes detectable.
Replace proportional prey capture with a saturating intake response at high prey abundance.
Introduce predator interference when predator density suppresses individual feeding rates.
Allow weak seasonal variation in prey reproduction if repeated cycles track a fixed environmental period.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of prey abundance
expected_behaviors: Prey abundance increases when predators are absent or sufficiently rare.
Predator abundance declines when prey are too scarce to offset natural losses.
Predator pressure reduces the prey growth rate.
For suitable parameter values and initial conditions, predator and prey peaks may recur with predator peaks lagging behind prey peaks.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative predator or prey abundance.
Predator reproduction in the complete absence of prey.
Predation that increases prey abundance.
Finite-time divergence of either population from finite nonnegative initial abundances.

scenario_text: A neuron is stimulated by a fixed current pulse while its membrane voltage and three voltage-dependent channel gates evolve over time. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of membrane-voltage change generated by capacitive charging, passive leakage, and opposing sodium-like and potassium-like ionic currents. Gate dynamics regulate channel availability and activation, producing a rapid voltage spike followed by repolarization. Ion concentrations, reversal potentials, membrane area, and stimulus amplitude remain fixed background conditions during each trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Capacitive membrane charging from the fixed applied current and net transmembrane ionic current.
Passive voltage-dependent leak current.
Fast regenerative inward current controlled by activation and availability gates.
Delayed outward current controlled by a voltage-dependent activation gate.
Voltage-dependent relaxation of each channel gate toward its admissible fraction.
baseline_assumptions: The neuron is represented as a single electrically uniform compartment.
Intracellular and extracellular ion concentrations remain constant over the trajectory.
Reversal potentials and maximal channel conductances are fixed.
Channel populations are large enough that gating can be treated deterministically.
scientific_constraints: Each gating state remains bounded between zero and one.
Outward potassium-like current opposes strong depolarization under the fixed ionic conditions.
Loss of sodium-like availability weakens the regenerative inward current.
The unstimulated system has a bounded resting state.
refinement_agenda: Add a slow adaptation current to capture spike-frequency accommodation.
Release the fixed-ion-concentration assumption to model activity-dependent reversal-potential shifts.
Add stochastic channel fluctuations for small membrane patches.
Add a second electrical compartment to represent dendrite-to-soma voltage coupling.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Instantaneous time derivative of the neuronal membrane voltage during stimulus-evoked spike generation.
expected_behaviors: A sufficiently strong fixed stimulus can initiate a rapid regenerative depolarization.
Sodium-like activation rises rapidly during depolarization while sodium-like availability declines.
Delayed potassium-like activation supports repolarization after the voltage peak.
After stimulation, the state tends back toward a stable resting regime.
forbidden_behaviors: Channel-gate fractions below zero or above one.
Unbounded membrane voltage under the stated fixed stimulus.
A voltage spike without voltage-dependent regenerative inward current.
Persistent voltage increase after inward-current availability has fallen and delayed outward activation is high.

scenario_text: A large diploid population carries two alleles at one autosomal locus, and genotypes differ in survival from zygote to reproductive adult. The sampled allele frequency and three genotype-specific relative survival values determine the allele frequency among survivors in a single generation. Genotype frequencies before selection are generated by random union of gametes, while mutation, migration, recombination, and genetic drift are absent. The benchmark target is the post-selection frequency of the focal allele.
baseline_mechanisms: Random pairing of alleles determines pre-selection genotype proportions.
Genotype-specific viability changes genotype contributions to the surviving population.
Allele counting among survivors determines the post-selection focal-allele frequency.
baseline_assumptions: The population is sufficiently large that random genetic drift is negligible.
Gametes unite randomly with respect to the focal locus.
Relative survival values are constant within the sampled generation and do not depend on genotype frequencies.
Mutation, migration, and sex-specific selection are absent.
scientific_constraints: The predicted allele frequency must remain within the closed interval from zero to one.
Surviving genotype contributions must be nonnegative.
Total genotype frequency among survivors must normalize to one.
A common positive rescaling of all genotype survival values must leave the prediction invariant.
refinement_agenda: Add recurrent mutation between the two alleles.
Add migration from a source population with a distinct allele frequency.
Allow genotype survival to depend on the current allele frequency.
Relax random gamete union by introducing nonrandom mating.
Introduce separate genotype survival values for females and males.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Frequency of the focal allele among reproductive adults after one episode of genotype-dependent viability selection

input_symbols.description: Frequency of the focal allele among zygotes before viability selection

expected_behaviors: The output remains between zero and one for all allowed inputs.
Equal survival values for all three genotypes leave the allele frequency unchanged.
Increasing focal-allele homozygote survival while holding other inputs fixed generally increases the post-selection focal-allele frequency.
Multiplying all three survival values by the same positive factor does not change the output.
forbidden_behaviors: Allele frequencies below zero or above one.
Dependence on the absolute scale shared by all genotype survival values.
Spontaneous allele-frequency change when all genotype survival values are equal.
Singular or undefined predictions within the stated input ranges.
